result:
Everything below is hand work, with no code run. As a check on my reading of the shared definitions, I reproduced by hand these rows of your disclosed table:

- (RATION-3, CANCEL-WAIT, HOLD) on D2(4,3): 8, 4, 12, 12, 28, jam.
- The cap on D2(4,3): 8, 8, 20; with FILLERS: 8, 8, 12.
- (FLOOR1, CANCEL-RETIRE, HOLD) on the two-knot start: 4, 6, 4, 12, 20.
- (FLOOR1, CANCEL-OFFSHOOT, HOLD) on D2(4,3): 8, 4, 16, 24.

Names on D2(4,3): J is a round-1 join, O a round-1 offshoot, c the round-2 offshoot of O, d an offshoot of c.

## What to fix before the freeze

1. **"Jammed at round 2" under (FLOOR1, CANCEL-RETIRE, HOLD) is not an end.** The J's retire in round 2, so in round 3 each O is alone and makes two offshoots. P7 is wrong or ill-posed for that law.
2. **Under holding with FLOOR1 the brood mixes two rounds.** A holder's children from two readings fall into one brood's roster at birth, and the plan joins them. The reference never makes that join. The registered cutoffs (1 to 3) show it only as an underbuild.
3. **P6's underbuild is true by the definition of "weaned"** and hides the real fault, which is scaffold item 4. A one-line repair exposes it, with a hand prediction of a mismatch at exactly 13 births.
4. **"Holder" is already the record's word** for a knot holding a distinction, and study two's title relies on that sense.
5. **Study two's P2 lumps three laws that I expect to come out three ways.** I prove it for FLOOR1 with CANCEL-OFFSHOOT, expect it to fail for FLOOR1 with CANCEL-RETIRE, and cannot settle RATION-3.
6. **Study two's P3 depends on which pair is written out**, and fails for the pair I exhibit.

## Study one

**1.1 The demand under the cap**
- The reading is right past the start under RELEASE, including in the waiters' recursion. A common knot of a waiter and a new knot would have to be a parent of both, and a parent that gave earlier is spent.
- At the start it is exact only under the start clause's own condition (no acting start knot meets a waiting one). The argument says "past the start" and is silent here; state the condition and assert it at run time for every start and law.
- Under (CAP-3, HOLD) the argument does not hold. A holder's older child that is still a member shares a met set with its newer child, and the reading leaves that group out. No registered start exercises this (the ring starts jam; the small starts have no short knot). Say so.
- The gate is a weak check of D. For an offshoot, D of 0, 1 or 2 all give f = 2. Compare D itself against the reference, and make sure the gate's complete rounds are computed through the plan, not through step 6 directly.
- Useful fact: with no group of three in the demand roster, D is the sum over parents of (holding − 1). So f depends only on the parents' holdings, and a partial brood cannot give a wrong f by itself.
- Also needed: the last round R is undefined under (CAP-3, CANCEL-WAIT, HOLD). The O's are members and not short for ever, so no part is all-short. Add "or in a part at rest".

**1.2 Fillers**
- The holdings-at-birth formula is right: only the fillers bar, and a barred place is never taken.
- The match rule is sound and worth keeping. The barred count is the only thing that detects a wrong D when f hides it.
- D is available to a serial law: it counts planned siblings, read from the brood's roster at birth, and is exact under R3. It is a lookahead on knots not yet made, the same one f already uses.

**1.3 Holding**
- The stopping rule is right. A reading with no birth and no retirement is a fixed point, and every other reading lowers total holdings or removes a member, so the recursion ends.
- The hand claim is right through round 3: c makes 3 offshoots, c is never weaned under the frozen guards, and all three underbuild through round 2. I also expect a match through round 1; R1's surplus-offshoot route is blocked because a short J's siblings all stay in the roster.
- One disclosed sentence is wrong for the reference. O is not "asked for the same two joins in every later reading". In round 4 the met set of c is {O, d1, d2, d3}, so O is asked for five and turns short. The sentence is true only of your reading.
- A mismatch appears in two places, neither reachable by the frozen runs:
  - **CANCEL-WAIT:** if c were allowed to act, each d would plan 3 − 2 = 1 offshoot. The reference gives none, because each d keeps one for its cancelled join with O.
  - **FLOOR1 on the two-knot start:** o1 (round 2) makes x in round 3 and y in round 4. The brood {x, y} plans a join (x, y), while the reference gives x two offshoots. At cutoff 3 this shows as an underbuild (x's second offshoot); at cutoff 4 it is a mismatch.
- The match rule needs a fix: x and y have the same parent and the same f but different rounds. "Least-numbered" then decides which one is within the cutoff. Register the order.

**1.4 Predictions**

| # | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| P1, P5 | Expect true; near to construction given 1.1. |
| P2 | Expect true, 7. Trace: 5 births spend knots 0 and 1; J01 reads short, then alone, and plans 3 offshoots (D = 2, f = 2); the reference has one such offshoot with f = 2; the second is birth 7. O holding 2 gives no shorter route. The small-start half holds by the fact in 1.1. |
| P3 | Cannot be checked from what I have (the start is not written out) and has no trace. The cap changes offshoots to 2 and joins with D < 3, so "exactly 13" is inherited, not derived. Trace it or mark the number open. |
| P4 | Expect 4. Only D2(6,3) tests it; on D2(4,3) four steps reach everything. |
| P6 | True, nearly by construction. |
| P7 | The cap half is true by construction. The CANCEL-RETIRE half fails if the reference stops at the jam (mismatch at birth 9), and is a real test if it runs on. |
| P8 | I would predict it: on the two-knot start under both FLOOR1 holding laws, match through rounds 1 and 2, underbuild through round 3. On D2(4,3) with CANCEL-OFFSHOOT, match through round 3; two-round parents come only at round 5 or 6. |

Two smaller points:
- The "RELEASE for HOLD" control cannot be rejected where no knot is short. Name the start it must be rejected on.
- P8 names "the cycle", which run 4 does not list.

**1.5 The owner's request**
- The literal request, the cap with holding, is vacuous on every registered start. Say so in the text.
- He named two stops; underbuild is a third. Stopping there without a repair is honest only if the text says the stop follows from the definition.
- A repair to register as a second law (the word "cleared" is a placeholder): a parent **has given** when it is no member, or when its own brood is all-cleared, every birth planned for it in every reading is made, and its part is at rest. A knot is **cleared** when every parent has given. R3′ is R3 with "cleared" for "weaned". It is identical to R3 under RELEASE.
- Hand prediction for R3′ under (RATION-3, CANCEL-WAIT, HOLD): match through round 2, mismatch through round 3 at exactly 13 births on D2(4,3) (8 + c + 3 d + one offshoot of d), and 15 on Ring(5,3).
- Add cutoff 4 on the small starts.

**1.6 Words**
- **Holder:** collides with the record (see item 4 above). Every member also "still holds" something, so "the roster of those that still hold" literally names the whole roster. Try "stayer" and "the waiters' and stayers' roster", after checking the stem.
- **At rest:** the same section uses "the rest" for a remainder, and the phrase is a mechanics term. Try "quiet".
- **Reading:** "The reading is a reading" uses two senses in four words. Keep "reading" for one pass over a part and "scaffold" for the other.

## Study two

**2.1 The look**
- Usable. State two choices: a distinction shared by two knots both at distance d is seen; two shared places leading to one unseen knot are not seen as such.
- Per place is right. It is equivalent to the per-knot version when the test is "some renaming moves the parent places off the parent places".
- Make the main kinds "parent" and "not parent". With three kinds, a start place against a child place counts as a failure, which is not the owner's question. Report that separately.

**2.2 Certification**
- Sound, with one trap: a separating quantity must be computed on the extracted look. Refinement run on the whole structure sees one step too far at the edge of the look.
- Report pairs within one structure, across rounds, and across starts separately. A pair across starts only shows the rule must know the start.

**2.3 Hand work**
- **(FLOOR1, CANCEL-OFFSHOOT, RELEASE), two-knot start: a confusable pair at every d.**
  - Every knot has three places. Each parent P with its pair u, v and their join j makes a cycle of four, and each of the four has one more shared place leading to another such cycle. The start pair A, B fits the same pattern.
  - After round R the structure is everything within R steps of {A, B} in that pattern.
  - On a1, the place shared with A (parent) and the place shared with j (child) are exchanged by the renaming that swaps A with j and fixes a1 and a2.
  - The pair is confusable exactly when d ≤ R − 2, so at d = 6 from round 8, and the separating distance is R − 1. Use this as planted check (b); it has an exact threshold.
  - The cycle of four does not help here: the common knot and the join both have three places.
- **(FLOOR1, CANCEL-RETIRE):** the join retires and keeps a barred place, which marks the bottom of every cycle. I expect a rule at distance 2 or 3.
- **(RATION-3, CANCEL-WAIT) on D2(4,3):** I could not exhibit a pair.
  - Every non-start knot has places = parents + 3, so the look shows each knot's number of parents.
  - Given those numbers, the parent relation is the only one with no loop. That is a whole-structure fact, not a bounded one.
  - A pair therefore needs a chain of 2d parent steps through the knot that reads the same reversed. I lean toward a rule existing on the population, with low confidence.
- **P2:** true for CANCEL-OFFSHOOT, false for CANCEL-RETIRE, open for RATION-3. Split it by law.
- **P3:** fails for my pair (a1 is one step from a start knot), and its verdict depends on the pair chosen.

**2.4 Populations**
- P1 is the owner's population. On it a rule will likely exist because every look reaches the live roster. P2 is needed, and say it is the thread's addition.
- Main artifact: under fast laws the 2,000-knot cap arrives before any look of 6 steps avoids both the start and the members. Report, per law and d, the number of chosen places whose look has no start knot and no member. A rule found with none of those shows nothing.
- A pair at distance 6 is not "a pair no bounded reading tells apart". Track one pair across rounds and report its separating distance as a function of the round.
- P7: expect none. In the example above the parent is always the knot nearer the start, and every whole-structure renaming keeps that.

**2.5 Predictions**
- P1 follows from P2 where P2 holds. Its "in P1" half can fail on tiny structures.
- P2 and P3 as above.
- P4 will mostly show the artifact.
- P5 to P7 are properly open.

**2.6 Words**
- **Look:** fine, and rightly not "view".
- **Agree:** LR already uses it for structures that match on knots including their parent sets. The shared definitions say "the same" for rosters up to renaming; use that or "alike".
- **Confusable pair:** fine, but it is a pair of places where the owner said pairs of knots; say so once.
- **Start place:** drop it to a sub-case of "not parent".
- **Spatial words:** "frontier" and "around" are still in the text.
- **Holder steps:** depends on the fix in 1.6.
